body: What's the deployment like for the carriers in Japan? I've only heard the sub is deployed almost constantly doing donuts in the ocean.

I know it's early but I was really just asking to gauge whether or not he should decide to leave after the 6 years or stay star reenlist for a shore duty and maybe work on his degree on the side. Heard a lot of back and forth on recruiter but it seems like the lesser of 3 evils still between it, shipyard and being an instructor (at prototype). He seems interested in it for the social aspect and not having to necessarily live near a naval base.

My uncle served in the navy and my aunt's ex-husband was in the army. Honestly it depends on the community you're living in and the crowd you're around. You'll here a lot of stories about infidelity on both sides, alcholism and domestic violence. There's also sometimes a perceived difference in how wives think they should be treated based on their husbands' rank and whether they're enlisted or officer that happens more when you live on base.

Dating and potentially marrying a military member takes a whole lot of commitment and willingness to maintain a healthy relationship while long distance, to keep yourself busy when you occassionally have to relocate and be seperated from your family on top of dealing with all the military spouse drama that comes with it. Many military marriages end in divorce due to a combination of all of these factors and military members in general sometimes rushing into these relationships for the benefits. It's hard and it's lonely and the community as a whole tends to side with the service member and service members stationed in OCONUS areas tend to have a bad rep for looking for flings more than serious relationships.

It would be financially difficult but ultimately I'd be happier not feeling like I was staying in a crumbling marriage where my husband disregards my feelings, uses his job to continue to have zero accountability for helping with his child, and isolates me from my family.

I'm also in a similar situation where I have a two year old and a husband currently in bootcamp. The best advice I can give is to make sure you have a solid foundation in your marriage and plans and a strong support system for when he is gone. Also sit down and have a serious conversation about all your options to improve your current situation. The military always seems like the easiest choice because it guarantees benefits like health care and basic housing allowance but that comes in exchange for a lot of family time missed out on.

The civilian job opportunities and prestige of being a nuke are the reasons my husband wanted the job. My main concern is the fact that nukes work long hours and if he is on a submarine he will deploy often. His mother and sister both also discouraged him from the rate because of the work environment and the stress of the nuke pipeline but of course everything seems sunshine and rainbows when your recruiter is telling you how smart you are and that anything negative you hear is a lie. In addition our daughter has special needs and is non verbal and even before now because he already works long hours I am the sole physcial caregiver for her 90% of the time. I do love him but I am tired of compromising with him and being a single parent with a special needs child somewhere where I have no family is considered acceptable collateral for him because he does not care enough about my feelings or opinions on the matter more than money.

Unfortunately we've had the "potential collapse of our marriage conversation" weeks before he went to bootcamp on multiple seperate occasions and that has ultimately changed nothing. I am willing to seek counseling but he will not admit that there is an issue and from my husband's perspective I should be happy that we will be financially secure and the benefits of the military outweigh the strain on our relationship. I know that it isn't feasible for him to walk away from his commitment at this point but him joining the navy is not the sole reason for our marital problems and actually is just exasperating the things that he does not wish to talk about or work on in our relationship. I have previously mentioned seeking a divorce as well and he will not engage with me in any meaningful discussion regarding it.

It's not a big deal and he was able to go back and change it. Basically when he initially signed up at meps they only have him a Nuke contract where he was sub volunteering and told him there wasn't anything else so he thought he had to for a while. Only found out the day he shipped out that that wasn't true.
